shortcut_name: Reducing functional indifference to terminal connectivity
evidence: The survivor names the priority vertices "terminals", initializes subset DP with "FULL = (1 << t) - 1", and handles "if t <= 1: print(0)". This is the standard Steiner-tree subset-DP formulation.
affordance_in_statement: Any real-valued function f that is indifferent to all of your activated transpositions is necessarily indifferent (as a logical consequence) to a transposition of coordinates a and b
removal_suggestion: The connectivity reduction is intrinsic to the task and cannot be removed without changing its meaning. To make it less immediately recognizable, re-present the same requirement through an indirect function-equivalence or permutation-generator scenario, avoiding explicit graph-like language about coordinate indices, activated transpositions, and connectivity. The single-terminal shortcut can likewise be left implicit rather than highlighted in the note.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that activated transpositions generate equivalence classes equal to connected components, so the minimum-cost solution is a minimum Steiner tree connecting all priority coordinates.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Any real-valued function f that is indifferent to all of your activated transpositions is necessarily indifferent (as a logical consequence) to a transposition of coordinates a and b

common_affordance: The logical consequence of invariance under selected transpositions is exactly connectivity of the selected-operation graph among all priority coordinates, yielding a Steiner-tree problem.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Used an unnecessarily expensive all-pairs Floyd-Warshall/closure approach and exceeded the time limit instead of using the more targeted Steiner-tree subset DP with shortest-path relaxation.
Mistakenly reduced the problem to an ordinary MST over the priority coordinates, ignoring that non-priority coordinates may serve as cheaper Steiner vertices.
Made the same MST reduction error: it connects only the priority vertices and cannot exploit useful intermediate coordinates.

recommended_edit: Re-present the equivalent invariance requirement indirectly as closure under a family of generators or function-identification rules, rather than explicitly describing coordinate transpositions as operations on indexed vertices. This is the only common affordance, although it is structural and cannot be eliminated while preserving the exact optimization problem.
regression_risk: An indirect presentation may make the intended graph structure harder for the already-defeated MST-based models to recognize, but it could also make their heuristic behavior unpredictable; the main risk is restoring a simpler-looking MST interpretation if the new wording emphasizes only pairwise priority relations.
